blocks.text: A specific inflection of a word (particularly a noun, pronoun, or adjective) depending on its function in the sentence.
The case used to indicate the subject—or agent—of a finite verb.
The grammatical case, chiefly applicable to nouns, used to express a relationship of origin or possession.
Case used to express direction towards an indirect object, the recipient or beneficiary of an action.
The case used to mark the immediate object (direct object) on which the transitive verb acts.
A noun case used to express means or agency.
A noun case serving as object of a preposition.
A way of categorizing nouns, pronouns, or adjectives according to the inflections they receive.
Exercises: the terms themselves, written from their English; then which term a definition describes; then the terms matched to their English. Review Terms, above, drills this lesson's terms.
